name: Regional Variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of focal or regional muscle weakness consistent with peripheral neuropathy
Electrophysiological evidence of demyelination or axonal damage in affected nerves
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal cell count
Exclusion of other causes of focal neuropathy such as compressive or metabolic etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence of neuropathy and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF findings may be absent early in disease course; electrophysiological studies are critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected regions
searchTerms: reduced or absent reflexes in limb
hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected area

common.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness progressing proximally in affected region
searchTerms: muscle weakness starting in hands/feet moving upward

common.symptomName: Mild sensory loss in affected dermatomes
searchTerms: mild loss of sensation in skin areas
slight sensory deficits in affected region

common.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction limited to affected region
searchTerms: abnormal sweating or blood flow in limb

occasional.symptomName: Cranial nerve involvement localized to one side
searchTerms: facial or head nerve symptoms on one side
muscle cramps in arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Mild neuropathic pain in affected region
searchTerms: mild nerve pain in affected area

rare.symptomName: Facial palsy contralateral to limb weakness
searchTerms: facial weakness opposite to limb weakness
one-sided facial droop opposite limb symptoms
extreme blood pressure and heart rate swings

laboratory: Elevated CSF protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation)
imaging: MRI may show nerve root enhancement in affected regions
other: Nerve conduction studies showing demyelination or axonal damage localized to affected nerves

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Chronic course over months to years

redFlags: Bilateral symmetric weakness suggesting classic GBS
Signs of systemic infection or vasculitis
references: Hughes RA, Cornblath DR. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2005 Nov 5;366(9497):1653-66.
Orphanet: Regional variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome - ORPHA:231416
